newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end choppy session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end choppy session slightly higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks scratched out slender gains on Thursday but for the second straight session saw a sharp early rally dissipate in the face of nervous selling pressure.
The Dow industrials gained 14 points to close unofficially at 7942. Broader indexes also edged higher and New York Stock Exchange advancers outpaced decliners by nearly five-to-four.
The session mirrored Wednesday's, with stocks bursting higher at the open in relief over tame inflation data, only to sharply reverse course later in the session.
Stocks got some support from the bond market, which rallied after the U.S. Labor Department reported the Consumer Price Index rose a mere 0.2 percent in July, in line with forecasts.

The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury dipped four basis points to 6.56 percent, but even at that level stands nearly a quarter point higher than the 6.33 percent registered on July 30, when the Dow stood at a then-record 8254.89.
"There were great expectations built into the market then," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "Just last week, people were talking about interest rates going to six percent."

With their interest rate hopes evidently on hold, investors displayed an edgy willingness to sell into any market strength, analysts said, and stocks continued to work through a choppy consolidation of neary 900-point spring and summer rally.

"This is the kind of consolidation that has to go on after a significant run-up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We went through a long period where there were just no down days."
"With rates at 6.50 (percent) or below, valuations had some room to grow," he added, "but above 6.50 and they start to look a little stretched."

Among individual issues, Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp fell 1-7/16 to 31-5/16 amid growing Wall Street concern that the federal probe of the company's Medicare billings could implicate higher-ups in the organization.

Kmart Corp rose 1-3/16 to 12-15/16 after the discount chain store became the latest retailer to report strong quarterly earnings. Morgan Stanley upgraded the shares to strong buy following release of the results.

Uniforce Services Inc jumped 6-1/2 to 29-15/16 after it agreed to accept a $32 per share cash and stock acquisition bid from fellow staffing service company Comforce Corp. Comforce shares fell 1/2 to 7-1/2.

Talbert Medical Management Holdings Corp gained 5-3/8 to 62-3/8. Talbert, a physician practice management company, agreed to be acquired by MedPartners Inc for $63 per share in cash. MedPartners rose 7/16 to 22-15/16.
The Standard & Poor's 500 rose 2.75 points to 924.77.
